step3.ptxt: The parts that make up the refrigerant cycle, the compressor oil, etc. are not interchangeable between HFC-134a (R134a) systems and conventional R12 systems.

item.ptxt: Under normal handling it is non-toxic and harmless, but it may change into a harmful gas when exposed to open flames or high temperatures (cigarettes, stoves, etc.).
Pay sufficient attention to ventilation and do not work in an enclosed area.
Never check for gas leaks using a halide torch type leak tester.

atten4.ptxt: The manifold gauge is dedicated to HFC-134a (R134a) to prevent incorrect charging.

If compressor oil for R12 is used in a HFC-134a (R134a) system, the compressor may lock due to poor lubrication, or refrigerant gas may leak due to swelling of rubber parts. Conversely, if compressor oil for HFC-134a (R134a) is used in a R12 system, the durability of the A/C system will decrease.

step3.ptxt: Compressor oil for HFC-134a (R134a) is highly hygroscopic, so when A/C parts are removed, immediately seal them from the atmosphere with plugs, vinyl tape, etc.
Compressor oil for HFC-134a (R134a) has an adverse effect on acrylic resin, so do not splash the oil.

atten4.ptxt: O-rings for HFC-134a (R134a) and O-rings for R12 differ in material, size, etc., so using the wrong ones may cause gas leaks.

step3.ptxt: When evacuating, attach a solenoid valve adapter to the vacuum pump for R12.

atten4.ptxt: If the system is left after evacuation without using a solenoid valve adapter, the oil (for R12) in the vacuum pump may flow back into the HFC-134a (R134a) system.

step3.ptxt: Inspect for refrigerant gas leaks using a halogen leak detector (ND part number 95146-00180).

item.ptxt: Conventional halide torch type leak testers cannot be used because HFC-134a (R134a) does not contain chlorine.
Conventional electric gas leak testers may also be unable to detect leaks due to low sensitivity, because the molecules of HFC-134a (R134a) are smaller than those of R12.

step3.ptxt: Perform the refrigerant gas leak inspection with the ignition switch OFF.

item.ptxt: If performed with the engine running, leaking gas is diluted by the air from the fan, blower, etc., making it difficult to detect.
If performed with the cooler operating, the refrigerant pressure in the cooler unit decreases, making gas less likely to leak.

If performed with the cooler operating, the electric gas leak tester may react to the sudden change in humidity caused by moist air from the drain hose (models compatible with HFC-134a (R134a), which are highly sensitive, are particularly likely to react) and give a false result.

step2.ptxt: If Refrigerant Gas Gets in the Eyes

step3.ptxt: Do not rub the eyes with a handkerchief or hands.

step2.ptxt: Precautions for Handling Refrigerant Gas (Service Cans)

step3.ptxt: Do not heat service cans. If a service can is heated directly or placed in boiling water, the pressure inside the can becomes abnormally high and the can may burst. If a service can must be warmed, use warm water of 40°C or less.
Do not drop or strike service cans.

Do not open the high pressure valve of the manifold gauge while the engine is running. If the high pressure valve is opened while the engine is running, high pressure gas may flow back into the service can and cause it to burst.
Do not handle service cans near your face. Also, always wear protective goggles.

item.ptxt: When removing O-rings, use a soft object such as a toothpick so as not to damage the pipe.

step3.ptxt: Apply sufficient compressor oil (ND-OIL8) to the O-rings.
Route hose piping naturally, without twisting or forcibly bending it.
Do not use cotton work gloves, etc., as lint or other foreign matter on the O-rings can cause refrigerant gas leaks.
